subject: Private offer — gross-to-net routing, invoice path and partner split
messages:

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer — gross-to-net routing, invoice path and partner split

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As promised I'm sending over the draft private-offer term sheet and a short note on questions we usually see from customers when a partner/reseller is in the flow. The attached term sheet shows list price and suggested passback model, but I want to confirm one detail before we lock: how would ClearRiver like us to handle gross-to-net and invoice routing when the end customer purchases via your reseller?

Two quick options that customers commonly pick (we can do either):
- Reseller pass-through: Redwood invoices reseller directly; reseller invoices end customer and retains agreed margin. Gross revenue recognized to Redwood is net of reseller pass-through.
- Channel uplift (Redwood invoices customer, we route a partner commission/settlement to the reseller): Redwood invoices end customer at list, Redwood pays partner commission according to waterfall.

For the private offer we need to decide routing because it affects the invoice paths, tax handling, and how marketplace credits/credits-back are applied. Can you confirm which approach your procurement/legal prefers? If neither, tell us the specific invoice path you need (example: reseller issues PO to ClearRiver, ClearRiver collects payment and nets reseller fee — we can try to match).

Attached: Private_Offer_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term economics + example invoice paths).

If helpful I can loop Ben from Marketplace Ops to map the exact invoice flow for your ERP.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: Private offer — gross-to-net routing, invoice path and partner split

Hannah,

Thanks for the term sheet. We reviewed with procurement and our finance lead — a couple of clarifying questions before we proceed to signature:

1) We prefer ClearRiver to be the billed party (we will issue the PO). We typically route reseller commissions on our side (we remit to the reseller after we receive invoice). Can Redwood support: Redwood invoices ClearRiver; ClearRiver pays Redwood and separately remits reseller commission? That is, Redwood would not be responsible for paying the reseller directly.

2) If Redwood requires paying the reseller, we need a clear channel margin waterfall on the private offer so our AP can reconcile. Please provide a sample waterfall showing list price -> marketplace fee -> reseller margin -> net payment to Redwood.

3) We operate in both US and EU; EU transactions require different VAT handling. Any change to partner commission % across territories?

4) Can we get an example invoice path (fields) that shows where partner id/partner PO number will appear? Our ERP needs that to automate remittances.

We attached our Channel_Routing_Requirements.xlsx with the fields our AP needs. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's faster.

Regards,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private offer — gross-to-net routing, invoice path and partner split

Hannah / Vanessa,

Looping in marketplace ops answers and a proposed dual-path approach we can offer to ClearRiver. Please feel free to copy/paste this to Marta with the attachments.

Short answers to Marta's points:
- Yes, we can issue invoices directly to ClearRiver (Redwood invoices ClearRiver). In that flow Redwood also supports sending partner commission statements to ClearRiver (so ClearRiver can remit to reseller). We call that "customer-billed, partner-managed commission". That incurs no extra handling by Redwood beyond including partner identifiers on the invoice and providing a monthly commission CSV.

- Alternatively, if ClearRiver prefers Redwood to pay the reseller, we support "Redwood-managed payout". In that case Redwood will issue the partner payment according to an agreed waterfall (below) and provide settlement remittance reports.

Proposed waterfall (example numbers, can be tuned):
1) List price charged to customer: $100.00
2) Marketplace fee (platform pass-through to marketplace): 6% -> $6.00
3) Partner commission (reseller margin): US: 12% -> $12.00 (EU: 10% -> $10.00)
4) Net revenue to Redwood before taxes/credits: $100 - $6 - $12 = $82.00 (US)

Notes:
- If Redwood pays the partner, we will reduce our recognized revenue per the waterfall and will send ClearRiver a monthly partner settlement CSV.
- VAT handling: in EU flows where reseller is VAT-registered, the invoice will show VAT separately; partner commission handling can be either grossed up or treated as a separate payable depending on reseller preference. We'll coordinate with your tax counsel if needed.

Invoice fields we will include (match to your sheet):
- InvoiceNumber, InvoiceDate, BillToCompany, BillToTaxID, PO_Number, Partner_ID, Partner_Name, Partner_ContractRef, LineItem (SKU, Qty, UnitPrice), MarketplaceFee, PartnerCommissionAmount, NetDue

Attached is a routing diagram (RoutingFlow_v2.drawio) showing two flows: A) Customer-billed / partner-managed commission (ClearRiver remits to reseller), B) Redwood-managed payout.

If ClearRiver wants Redwood to handle payout, we will need reseller W9/W-8 or EU tax docs and a signed partner addendum. If they want to remit themselves, we only need confirmation of Partner_ID to appear on invoice and a monthly commission.csv template.

Ben

Hi Marta — thank you and appreciate the clear checklist. Per Ben's note above, both flows are supported. Summary and next steps: 

Summary options (pick one):
A) Customer-billed / partner-managed commission (recommended if ClearRiver wants to control remittances): Redwood invoices ClearRiver. Invoice contains Partner_ID + Partner_Name in a dedicated field. Redwood provides a monthly PartnerCommission.csv for reconciliation; ClearRiver remits to reseller. No Redwood payout required.

B) Redwood-managed payout: Redwood invoices ClearRiver at list, deducts marketplace fee and partner commission from Redwood's remittance ledger, and issues payment to reseller. Redwood will produce monthly settlement reports and will require reseller tax docs and a partner addendum.

Territory notes: partner commission % in our proposal is 12% (US) / 10% (EU) by default; we can negotiate regionally. EU VAT will be shown and handled per your tax guidance — we'll coordinate with your tax team.

Requested items from your side to finalize and generate DocuSign:
- Confirm which flow (A or B) you prefer
- Confirm Partner_ID(s) to appear on invoice (one line per reseller)
- Confirm EU reseller tax docs if you want Redwood to pay them (flow B)

If you confirm flow A, we can finalize a 1-page addendum and send for signature today; that addendum documents invoice fields and reporting cadence (monthly CSV). If you confirm flow B, we'll prepare the payout addendum and request reseller W-9/W-8 or EU equivalent before DocuSign.
